In the 47 defendants case, 12 defendants lodged appeals, which were rejected by the Court of Appeal in February this year. Among them, 11 subsequently applied to the Court of Appeal for a certificate of leave to appeal to the Court of Final Appeal. The Court of Appeal will announce its decision next Monday (the 10th), with the process expected to take five minutes.

In February this year, the Court of Appeal dismissed the appeals of 12 defendants.

In the 47 defendants case, 45 defendants were convicted of conspiracy to subvert state power. Among them, 12 — namely Avery Ng, Claudia Mo, Sidney Ng, Yu Wai-ming, Gwyneth Ho, Lam Cheuk-ting, Ng Ching-hang, Cheng Tat-hung, Ho Kai-ming, Jimmy Sham, Leung Kwok-hung, and Wong Tsz-yuet — had earlier lodged appeals, all of which were dismissed in late February this year. The Department of Justice's appeal against Lau Wai-chung's acquittal was also dismissed.

Excluding Wong Tsz-yuet, 11 defendants applied to appeal to the Court of Final Appeal, seeking a certificate of leave to appeal from the Court of Appeal. The 11 were sentenced to imprisonment ranging from 78 to 93 months. Among them, Gwyneth Ho appealed against her conviction, while the other 10 appealed against both conviction and sentence. According to the Judiciary's website, the Court of Appeal will announce its decision next Monday (the 10th), with the process expected to take five minutes.

The Court of Appeal dismissed the appeals of the 12 in February this year, ruling that the trial judge's finding that the defendants were members of the conspiracy was 'unassailable.' However, regarding whether the Basic Law permits legislators to force the Chief Executive to be held accountable by vetoing the financial budget, the Court of Appeal considered the question to be of significant constitutional importance, but noted that the parties' submissions were 'sketchy' and declined to make a ruling. On sentencing, the Court of Appeal also held that the starting point of seven years' imprisonment was not manifestly excessive, and endorsed the sentence passed at trial.
